message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Build Mod

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  buildJar:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up PATH
        run: |
          echo "${ANDROID_HOME}/build-tools/34.0.0" >> $GITHUB_PATH
      - name: Set up JDK 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v5
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: 17
      - name: Cache Gradle packages
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.gradle/caches
            ~/.gradle/wrapper
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-${{ hashFiles('**/build.gradle', '**/gradle.lockfile') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-
      - name: Build mod jar
        run: |
          chmod +x ./gradlew
          ./gradlew deploy
      - name: Upload built jar file
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          archive: false
          name: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}
          path: build/libs/${{ github.event.repository.name }}.jar",
  "rationale": "The workflow is a Gradle/Java build that re-downloads dependencies on every run. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-cache pattern (supported by experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9) applies because repeated dependency fetching is measurable and no equivalent cache exists. Adding an actions/cache step for ~/.gradle/caches and ~/.gradle/wrapper, keyed on build.gradle and gradle.lockfile, preserves all build/test steps and required coverage without weakening permissions, adding secrets, or introducing deployment/publishing or new network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9"]
}
